key_insight: Embedding exact boundary and initial constraints in a PINN enables accurate identification of the shear piezoelectric coefficient e15 from sparse, noisy simulated wavefields.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support non-destructive characterization of shear-mode coupling in PMUTs and surface acoustic wave devices.
method: Embed spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers to enforce clamped, grounded boundaries and a resting initial state exactly.
Train on coupled electro-elastodynamic equations and sparse observations without boundary or initial-condition penalty weights.
Non-dimensionalize the equations to balance governing coefficients near order one.
evidence_signal: On finite-element data sampled along one subsurface line, the full formulation achieved 1.19% mean e15 error at 30 dB noise and 0.65–2.71% across a 40–0 dB noise sweep.
watch_item: Validation is limited to simulated data; performance on physical devices with model mismatch and uncertain boundary conditions remains untested.
paper_title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
